ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure contains an upper component and a lower component, with a reaction arrow/curved arrow in the middle; the upper component is a positively charged pyridinium ring, connected to a fragment containing a C=C side chain, an R substituent, and OH, and there is also Br− beside it; the lower component is an R1-substituted alkene connected to a carbonyl and bearing an R2 substituent. Reasoning count: According to the meaning of the problem, exclude all bonds involving hydrogen, exclude arrows, and also do not count Br− as a bond. Upper component: around the pyridinium ring there are 6 non-hydrogen bonds, N to side-chain carbon has 1 bond, side-chain C=C counts as 1 bond, C-R counts as 1 bond, C-O counts as 1 bond, 10 non-hydrogen bonds in total. Lower component: R1-C counts as 1 bond, C=C counts as 1 bond, the C-C connection from the alkenyl carbon to the carbonyl carbon counts as 1 bond, C=O counts as 1 bond, and carbonyl carbon to R2 C-R2 counts as 1 bond, 5 non-hydrogen bonds in total. The total number is 10 + 5 = 15.

method.method_draft: Describe the image, then count bonds by regions. Upper component: count the six bonds around the pyridinium ring, the bond from N to the side-chain carbon, the C=C bond in the side chain, the C-R bond, and the C-O bond, giving 10 non-H bonds. Do not count O-H, Br−, or arrows. Lower component: count R1-C, C=C, C-C carbonyl connection, C=O, and C-R2, giving 5 non-H bonds. Add 10 + 5 to obtain 15.
